Q177: Easiest to use was Design B because it used colors to denote the instances when the machines were functioning outside of range.  Furthermore, the most recent output amount was denoted with a number, but the number did not fluctuate in size, so it was easy to read.  I would like for that design to be improved by putting the most recent/current output amount in a box, have the font and the box be the same size for any output number, but color the box blue if the current output is too low or orange if the current output is too high.  This would aid in readability and efficiency.  I also think Design B should implement the gray band to show the acceptable range because that also makes the visual message clearer.  The worst design elements were when the graph used no color whatsoever to help the viewer distinguish facts from one another, as well as when the size of the box containing the most recent output amount would fluctuate.  The small boxes were much harder to read than the large ones.  This is especially bad because I imagine a factory would want output to be higher than lower, so such an issue should be addressed quickly.  I think Design E would be the best out of all of the designs if it implemented the blue and orange colored dots on the graphs, if it used blue/orange to denote that the most recent output number is too low or too high, and if the box containing the output number did not change in size.
Feedback: The instructions for this survey were very clear.
